name: Adam Schiff
stance: Wants enforceable, industry-wide guardrails on frontier AI, a dedicated expert AI regulator, company transparency with Congress, and vigorous oversight of rogue-agent episodes.

statements.text: My new bill would protect Americans from unlawful domestic surveillance and insist that humans make the final decision on the use of force by autonomous weapons systems.
Announced a bill with Sen. Banks and Reps. Latta and Whitesides allowing information-sharing among U.S. AI labs to counter AI distillation attacks and other foreign security threats.
And I think it’s fair to ask whether Congress is asleep at the wheel as we hurtle towards AGI and the unknown.

Legislation is necessary to make this a requirement of all companies, not simply those who agree to do so, to ensure the requisite of these monitors, and that the companies properly and safely pace new developments.
But regulation and legislation should not be used to lock in monopolies, bypass important state laws or give broad exemptions that lock out a competitive landscape for decades to come.
The CEOs of OpenAI and Anthropic came together this past week to warn how AI could destroy humanity within a decade.

We need formalized international coordination and communication — with China and other countries — to ensure the push to develop and diffuse the most capable AI models does not cause catastrophic consequences for humanity.
AI agents have colluded, escaped their sandboxes, hacked other companies, meddled with government portals — and that's just the ones we know about.
When AI undermines our national security, a pinky swear won't cut it.

Called for enforceable industry-wide guardrails against the harms of frontier AI and for a regulatory body with the expertise and discretion to keep pace with advanced models, and promised vigorous oversight of rogue AI-agent episodes.

there is a real national security threat here. As these models become more and more advanced, as they advance themselves through this recursive AI, we have less and less of a sense of what they're doing, how they're deciding what they're deciding

we're going to need a regulatory body that has real discretion and real expertise that can move a lot quicker than Congress can. Whether that looks like an FDA for artificial intelligence or some other agency, I think that's ultimately going to be necessary.
The threat of rogue AI agents taking unauthorized actions within our financial institutions, utilities, health systems and more has long since stopped being a hypothetical.
